items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I received from Peter O’Brian [spelling?]. In there was this tune called “Mary’s Waltz”

ctx.x: And also Cecil Taylor. Did you know . . . I know you know Cecil. Did you know Herbie Nichols very well or at all?

I never did. I didn’t know much about his music. I just knew him, because he died quite a few years ago, didn’t he? I think the most I’ve heard about Herbie Nichols is that Geri Allen made a point of playing a lot of his music. Through that . . . He did some playing with or working with or composing for or something with Mary Lou Williams, because I had a tune which allegedly was written by Mary Lou in this whole bunch of tunes that I received from Peter O’Brian [spelling?]. In there was this tune called “Mary’s…
Yeah, he actually got here in the late ’50s, but his impact was more the ’60s.
